The story is almost an exact mirror of my personal journey into Arizona to buy a vintage Mercedes-Benz. The moment the front wheels of my vehicle crossed the Pima county line heading to Tucson, me and my friend were suddenly thrown into a brutal fight for survival. We practically crawled our way to Tucson, fighting tooth and nail against the scum that choose to live in such a wretched city. The locals we encountered and escaped bore a frightening resemblance to the enemies found in this game. Our journey reached its peak when we finally arrived at the place in which our seller decided to have us meet. A massive warehouse in an industrial zone, gated and heavily monitored. Minutes turned into hours while we waited for the seller, chucking nickels and pennies at oncoming locals. When he finally came, he arrived in a customized BMW motorcycle, it was modified so that the bike practically wrapped around his lower area in a U shape to support his massive, fat, greasy body. As he rolled off the motorcycle the locals stopped and bowed down and he beckoned two of the frailest, sunburnt individuals I’ve seen to open the gates to his warehouse. My friend and I waited in intense anticipation as he waddled to the front door of the warehouse to unlock it. As he did the locals began to gather behind him in awe. After long anticipation he swung the warehouse doors open and to our sight were at least 90 Mercedes-Benz vehicles in absolute pristine condition, wall to wall, floor to ceiling in some areas. As we gazed upon a collectors wet dream, the seller screamed into the gathering crowd of decrepits “I WANT THE CLEANEST ONE OF YOU”. Out came a gorgeous woman in a dirtied dress, she presented herself and bowed to the seller. “What do you ask?” and he screamed for her to get the black 1991 W140 for us. I really wanted to like Outlast 2. The first game had such a tight, terrifying atmosphere, and I was hoping for more of that here. Unfortunately, what I got was a disjointed experience that left me more frustrated than scared.

The biggest issue? The pacing. Outlast 2 throws you into relentless chase sequences over and over again, with very little breathing room. Tension builds best when there's a mix of quiet moments and terror, but here it's like the game forgot that horror isn't just about being constantly hunted.

Then there's the story. I appreciate that they aimed for something deeper with themes of religion and cult fanaticism, but the execution felt messy. The narrative jumps around in confusing ways, and by the end, I felt like I had more questions than answers without the satisfying kind of ambiguity. It’s hard to stay invested when you’re not sure what’s really going on half the time.

The gameplay also felt trial-and-error heavy, especially during chase scenes. Dying repeatedly because you didn’t know which way to run isn’t scary; it’s just irritating. I don’t mind difficult games, but when difficulty comes from clunky design rather than player skill, it gets old fast.

On a positive note, the visuals and sound design are top-notch. The environments are genuinely creepy, and the atmosphere does a great job of setting a dark, hopeless tone. But sadly, that wasn’t enough to keep me hooked.

If you’re into horror games purely for the atmosphere, you might enjoy it. But if you want a well-paced, engaging horror experience, Outlast 2 just doesn’t live up to its predecessor.

Outlast 2 is a much higher production value, ambitious sequel to Outlast. There's immersion improvements, e.g. you are told when to record events, being able to review your footage (including notes) via the camera, real time inventory screen straight out of Alone in the Dark 2008. Gameplay improvements like limited stamina and the need to bandage yourself after being hit with bandages you scavenge like batteries. Several references to horror movies, e.g. Nightmare on Elm Street, or The Shining. The atmosphere, when allowed to build up, can be fairly thick.

Those are the good things. The bad things are many, unfortunately.
Instant kill enemies, enemies that spawn alerted in the only doorway of the room so you have to take damage to progress, enemy AI that knows exactly where you are at all times forcing you to just forgo any stealth gameplay and leg it. Scripted trial & error sequences where you have to guess what the developers want you to do. Flashback/hallucination sections that make the camera have a nauseous wavy effect.
You'll be lost multiple times looking for a crawl space in the corner, or a space where you can squeeze through sideways. They're marked by bloodied hands, but they're not easily discernible in night vision, which you'll be using 90% of the time due to how dark the game is. This issue is especially egregious during chase scenes. The level designers fail time and time again in directing the player across the map. What's worse, near the end of the game it's chase after chase after chase.

Outlast 2 is even more edgy than the last one. In my review of Outlast 1 I had hoped that the second game has baby eating to outdo it, but it blows its load too early with mass infanticide in the first 30 minutes. There is nothing that tops this later on. 
It has questionable writing. Outlast 1's story is simple, but it does its job. Outlast 2's is an incoherent mess, deliberately so, in order to make it seem more clever than it actually is. Most notes you find are just flavor text, some are extremely lengthy backstories written like Bible passages which makes deciphering them problematic, and there is a single easy-to-miss note which... explains nearly everything in simple terms, if you know Outlast lore. But to fully understand the plot, you still need to watch a YouTube video.

Oh yeah, and jumpscares are so loud they burst your ear drums.

Outlast knows it's a gore horror movie and revels in it. Outlast 2 is a gore horror movie that thinks it's sophisticated enough to have a message, i.e. religion is bad. If you want hillbilly enemies with violence and gratuitous gore in a horror game which is actually good, play Resident Evil 7.
